name: Water vs Eva Water
desc: What you drink is the most-used input to the body. Tap is regulated for safety, not for vitality — heavy metals, chlorine, microplastics, and lost molecular structure. Eva is structured-water purification: filters the contamination, then restores molecular coherence. The closest a domestic appliance gets to drinking from a real spring.

name: White Oak Pastures
desc: Family-owned regenerative farm in Bluffton, Georgia. Whole-animal butchery, holistic grazing, carbon-positive at the farm scale. The clearest US example of meat as medicine when raised on healthy land.

name: Frantoio Franci
desc: Tuscan single-estate olive oil, cold-extracted within hours of harvest. The benchmark for what extra-virgin olive oil should taste like — peppery, alive, traceable to a single grove.

name: Manuka Health
desc: UMF-certified raw Manuka honey from New Zealand. Antibacterial, traceable, third-party-tested. Honey that still does what honey is supposed to do.

name: Dr. Bronner's Pure-Castile Soap
desc: Family-owned for five generations, fair-trade certified, organic, biodegradable. Eighteen uses on one bottle. The simplest soap that actually does the job, with a label worth reading.

name: Bite Toothpaste Bits
desc: Fluoride-free toothpaste tablets in a refillable glass jar. Plastic-free, simple ingredients, no surfactants you cannot pronounce. The cleanest mainstream alternative to the tube.

name: Native Deodorant
desc: Aluminum-free, paraben-free deodorant with a transparent ingredient list. Effective without the trade-offs the conventional formulas ask of the lymphatic system.

name: Boie Toothbrush
desc: Antimicrobial bristles, BPA-free, designed to outlast a normal toothbrush by a factor of six. Less plastic in landfills, gentler on enamel.

name: American Express Platinum
desc: The traveller's card. Lounge access, hotel and airline credits, concierge that actually picks up. Annual fee is steep — works only if you actually move through the world.

name: Crypto.com Visa
desc: Spend crypto like cash. CRO-staking tiers unlock cashback, streaming-service rebates, and metal cards. The on-ramp for using digital assets in everyday purchases.

name: Mercury
desc: Banking and cards built for the kind of company you actually want to run. Free, fast, sane API, no monthly fees, no minimum balance. The first business banking experience that does not feel like a relic.

name: Apple Card
desc: Designed by Apple, issued by Goldman. Daily Cash on every purchase, no fees, full transparency in how you spend. Privacy-first by design — Apple cannot see your transaction-level data. The cleanest mainstream card for anyone already inside the ecosystem.

name: Wise Multi-Currency Card
desc: Hold and spend 40+ currencies at the real mid-market exchange rate. The card and account that ended the era of being quietly robbed by your bank's FX margin. The default for anyone who actually crosses borders.

name: Revolut
desc: European challenger bank built for the post-border generation. Multi-currency accounts, fee-free transfers up to a limit, crypto, stocks, vaults — all in one app. The default account for anyone moving between Berlin, Lisbon, and London.

name: Charles Schwab High-Yield Investor Checking
desc: The traveller's secret. No foreign-transaction fees. Every ATM fee on Earth is refunded at the end of the month — Tokyo, Lima, Berlin, anywhere. Paired with Wise this is the cleanest cross-border setup that exists.

name: Bilt Rewards Mastercard
desc: Earn points on rent — the only card that does. No annual fee, transferable to airline and hotel partners, dining and travel rewards on everything else. The rare card built for the renter rather than the owner.

name: Oura Ring
desc: The canonical sleep and recovery tracker. Finnish-built titanium, no monthly subscription required for the basics, the most validated sleep-staging algorithm on the wrist. The first wearable that actually changed how a generation thinks about rest.

name: Avocado Green Mattress
desc: GOTS-certified organic, made in California from natural latex, organic cotton, and wool. Carbon-neutral company, 25-year warranty. The mattress that set the bar for what a mattress should be made of.

name: Coyuchi Sheets
desc: Organic cotton, GOTS-certified, fair-trade. The first US bedding company built for actually-clean fibres. Sheets that get softer for a decade rather than wear thin in two years.

name: Manta Sleep Mask
desc: The mask that actually blocks 100% of light without pressing on the eyelids. Adjustable eye-cups, modular, durable. Worth more on the road than any pillow.

name: Hostage Tape
desc: Mouth tape — sounds odd until you try it. Forces nasal breathing through the night, which means deeper sleep, less snoring, less morning brain-fog. Niche, then non-negotiable.

name: AeroPress Original
desc: The most durable coffee tool ever made. Plastic but the good kind — BPA-free, lifetime build. Travel anywhere with it. The cleanest cup of coffee you can make with thirty seconds of effort.

name: Niche Zero Grinder
desc: Single-dose, conical burrs, near-zero retention. Engineered in the UK by people who actually drink coffee. The grinder that ended the era of compromising on the most important variable.

name: Fellow Stagg EKG Kettle
desc: Precision pour, exact temperature, gooseneck spout. Design as care. The kettle that turned a kitchen-counter object into a daily small ritual.

name: Heart Roasters
desc: Portland micro-roaster, single-origin only, light roasts that taste like the farm they came from. The benchmark for what specialty coffee is supposed to be.

name: Rishi Tea
desc: Whole-leaf loose tea, traceable to the garden, organic where the farm allows it. The first US tea company to take leaf quality seriously at scale.

name: Le Creuset Dutch Oven
desc: Enameled cast iron from a French foundry that has been making the same pot since 1925. Buy one in your twenties, hand it to your grandchildren. The warranty is essentially forever.

name: Lodge Cast Iron Skillet
desc: American-made since 1896. Thirty dollars. Functions perfectly for fifty years if you treat it right. The most overdelivering piece of cookware in the world.

name: Misono UX10 Chef Knife
desc: Japanese, hand-finished, takes an edge sharper than most home cooks need. The knife that closes the gap between expensive Japanese steel and what a serious cook actually requires.

name: Smithey No. 12 Skillet
desc: Polished cast iron from Charleston, SC. Mirror-smooth interior — the kind of finish your grandmother's pan got from forty years of seasoning, ready out of the box.

name: Boos Block Cutting Board
desc: American maple, made in Effingham, Illinois since 1887. Heavy, end-grain, a board that gets better with each year of oil. The piece of kitchen furniture you sharpen knives on for decades.

name: Manduka PRO Yoga Mat
desc: The standard. Cushioned, dense, thick enough for the knees. Lifetime guarantee. The mat every serious yoga teacher recommends without thinking about it.

name: Halfmoon Meditation Cushion
desc: Zafu and zabuton set, made in Vancouver since 1980. Buckwheat fill, organic cotton, the right height for actually sitting still. Built to last decades of daily use.

name: Theragun Pro
desc: The recovery tool athletes and serious practitioners actually use. Five attachments, professional-grade torque, sixteen-millimeter amplitude. Replaces a massage therapist for the daily maintenance work.

name: Sandalwood Mala
desc: 108 hand-strung sandalwood beads, traditionally used to count breaths or mantras. The simplest practice tool that has survived three thousand years for a reason.

name: Himalayan Singing Bowl
desc: Hand-hammered seven-metal bowl from Nepal, sourced from artisan families who have made them for generations. The sound itself is the practice.

name: 1Password
desc: Family-owned, zero-knowledge architecture, the password manager security professionals actually trust. The single most leveraged tool in your digital life.

name: Mullvad VPN
desc: Swedish, accepts cash, no email required to sign up. The only major VPN that has been independently audited and refused to comply with overreach. Costs five euros a month forever.

name: Proton Mail
desc: Swiss, end-to-end encrypted, jurisdiction matters. The cleanest mainstream alternative to Gmail. Pairs with Proton Drive and Proton VPN for a full sovereign stack.

name: Ledger Nano X
desc: Hardware wallet for self-custodying crypto. Bluetooth, secure element, supports thousands of assets. The recommended starting point for actually owning your keys.

name: Brave Browser
desc: Private by default. Blocks trackers, blocks fingerprinting, opts you out of the surveillance economy without a configuration step. The browser the rest should have been.

name: Pure Encapsulations Magnesium Glycinate
desc: The form of magnesium that actually absorbs without sending you to the bathroom. Pure Encapsulations is the brand functional medicine doctors hand to their own patients — no fillers, third-party tested.

name: Nordic Naturals Ultimate Omega
desc: Sustainably sourced fish oil, third-party tested for heavy metals and oxidation. The omega-3 supplement with the most independent verification of what is actually in the bottle.

name: Thorne Vitamin D/K2
desc: The canonical pairing. D3 without K2 deposits calcium in the wrong places. Thorne is the supplement brand US Olympic teams use for a reason — every batch tested, every ingredient traceable.

name: Sun Potion
desc: Single-ingredient adaptogens — pine pollen, ashwagandha, mucuna, He Shou Wu. Sourced from Daoist herbalists, no proprietary blends. The clean entry point into the herbal tradition.

name: Four Sigmatic Functional Mushrooms
desc: Lion's mane, reishi, cordyceps, chaga — the four mushrooms most people benefit from. Dual-extracted, organic, third-party verified. The brand that took medicinal mushrooms mainstream.

name: Leuchtturm 1917 Notebook
desc: Every page numbered, lays flat, archive-grade paper. The notebook bullet-journalers, designers, and second-brain people use. Made in Germany since 1917.

name: Lamy 2000 Fountain Pen
desc: Bauhaus design from 1966, manufactured identically today. Makrolon body, gold nib, the pen that has outlasted every design trend that came after it.

name: Leatherman Wave+
desc: 17 tools in one folding multitool. Made in Portland, Oregon, 25-year warranty, rebuildable. The tool you keep in the glove compartment that ends up doing fifty things you did not plan for.

name: Patagonia Black Hole 32L
desc: The duffel everyone has, for a reason. Recycled ripstop, weatherproof, lifetime repair through Patagonia's Worn Wear program. The travel bag that survives airports and outlives airlines.

name: Klean Kanteen
desc: Steel water bottle, no plastic, BPA-free, virtually unbreakable. American-owned, climate-neutral certified. The one bottle that earns the years of use it gets.

name: AirPods Pro 2
desc: Transparency mode, active noise cancellation, USB-C charging. The wireless earbuds that ended the argument. Daily-use audio for anyone in the Apple ecosystem.

name: Sennheiser HD 660S2
desc: Open-back wired headphones from the company that has been making reference monitors for 80 years. The standard for actually listening to music — the way the engineer heard it.

name: KEF LSX II Wireless Speakers
desc: British-engineered, Uni-Q driver array, audiophile sound in a desktop form factor. The speakers that hold their own against systems ten times their size.

name: Loop Earplugs
desc: Designed earplugs that lower volume without muffling clarity. Versions for concerts, focus, sleep, and conversation. Sound protection for the world we actually live in.

name: Hatch Restore
desc: Sunrise alarm, bedside light, white-noise machine, smart-free. The reason you no longer keep a phone next to the bed. Wake up to light instead of a ring.
